    Learn about buying property in Cambridge

    • What are the best areas to live in Cambridge, UK?
      Cambridge offers a mix of historic charm and modern convenience. Some of the most sought-after areas include:
      • Newnham – Picturesque and popular with academics and families.
      • Trumpington – Rapidly developing with good transport links.
      • Chesterton – Close to Cambridge North station, ideal for commuters.
      • De Freville Avenue – Prestigious location with period homes.
      • Queen Edith's – Excellent schools and near Addenbrooke's Hospital.
    • What is the average asking price for a family home in Cambridge?
      As of recent data:
      • Terraced houses – £600,000+
      • Semi-detached houses – £700,000+
      • Detached houses – £1.2 million+
    • How much does it cost to buy a house in Cambridge?
      The average property price is around £550,000, with variations depending on type and location.
    • Is Cambridge a good place to invest in property?
      Yes! Cambridge has strong rental demand, a growing economy, and excellent transport links to London, making it a prime investment location.
    • What are the main factors driving house prices in Cambridge?
      The main factors driving house prices in Cambridge include:
      • The University of Cambridge attracts students and international buyers.
      • Tech and biotech sectors (Silicon Fen) boost demand.
      • Top-rated schools make it desirable for families.
      • Transport improvements like Cambridge North station increase connectivity.
    • Are there any new property developments in Cambridge?
      New property developments in Cambridge include:
      • Eddington – Sustainable development by the University.
      • Trumpington Meadows – Modern homes with green spaces.
      • Northstowe – A new town outside Cambridge.
      • Darwin Green – Major family-friendly housing development.
    • What impact does the university have on the property market?
      The University of Cambridge creates consistent rental demand, attracts international buyers, and supports a high-income workforce, keeping property values high.
    • Are there restrictions on building extensions or renovations in Cambridge?
      Yes, especially in conservation areas and for listed buildings. Check with Cambridge City Council's planning department before making changes.
    • What are the best schools in Cambridge?
      The best schools in Cambridge include:
      • State Schools: Hills Road Sixth Form, Parkside Community College.
      • Primary Schools: Newnham Croft, Milton Road Primary.
      • Private Schools: The Leys, St. Faith's, King's College School.
    • How good is public transport and commuting in Cambridge?
      Cambridge has great train links to London (~50 minutes), a well-connected bus network, and the UK's best cycling infrastructure.
